newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand plays down Australian report jibes.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand plays down Australian report jibes.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Monday played down unflattering comments about his country contained in a secret Australian report on its Pacific neighbours.

At the same time Australian Minister of Defence Industry Bronwyn Bishop sought to limit the damage from the report, which criticises New Zealand for its "growing dependence on Australia", especially in defence and trade.
"The briefing paper does not represent government policy or government attitude," Bishop, in New Zealand for the commissioning of an Australian-built frigate, told reporters.

Bolger told a radio interviewer, "From an Australian point of view it is very embarrassing. From a New Zealand perspective I think we will be charitable and treat it as the view of a low-level official within the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade in Australia and leave it at that."

The top secret paper -- marked AUSTEO, or Australian eyes only -- was prepared by officials for Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, who hosted a summit of economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum in Cairns earlier this month.
Left on a hotel table where a Reuters journalist picked it up, the document said New Zealand does not have an equal relationship with Australia in terms of defence and trade.

"New Zealand's growing dependence on Australia, especially in CER (Closer Economic Relations) and defence -- in which New Zealand capacity is weak and declining -- underlines the strategic inequality of the relationship," the paper stated.
As a result of this supposed imbalance, Wellington tends to make external policy "gestures" that signal its freedom of action and sometimes frustrate Australian diplomacy, it said.

Bishop repeatedly declined to comment on the document's contents at a news conference other than to say it did not reflect her government's policy, and she stressed the importance of the relationship between Australia and New Zealand.
"It's a very important relationship where under CER and closer defence relations we have a very strong commitment to each other," she said.
"I can only say to you that I regard our relationship as a strong one, that it is a secure one in the sense that it's good not only for each other but it's good for the region as well."
The paper, which outlines embarrassing personal habits of the South Pacific Forum guests, also branded New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters an opportunist and a loose cannon.
Bishop said she had always found Peters to be a statesman.
"Winston Peters has behaved like a statesman, and I think has shown himself to be a statesman for your country," she said.
Peters made conciliatory remarks about the leak at the weekend.
Bolger is due to fly to Australia on Friday for a brief visit, centred around an international rugby match on Saturday, and is scheduled to meet his counterpart John Howard.
Finance Minister Bill Birch will also make the trip, with Birch due to meet Costello at the end of a busy week of bilateral engagements.

The frigate Te Kaha, due to be formally commissioned on Tuesday, is the first of two ANZAC-class warships built in Australia for the Royal New Zealand Navy, and New Zealand has an option to buy two more.
Australia has in the past expressed its desire for New Zealand to spend more on defence.
